title: Ashutosh Dixit Takes Charge as 29th IAF Chief Amid Modernisation Push
excerpt: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit succeeded A.P. Singh on October 31 after serving as Vice Chief, taking over the Indian Air Force during a programme of new aircraft, air defence and indigenous manufacturing.
body:
• Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on October 31, 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh.
  • Singh superannuated after 42 years of service, according to the Ministry of Defence release issued through the Press Information Bureau.
  • Dixit was commissioned into the IAF fighter stream on December 6, 1986, and was serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff immediately before taking charge.
  • He takes over while the IAF pursues modernisation covering new combat aircraft, air defence, indigenous manufacturing and advanced technologies, according to India Strategic.

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force on October 31, 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who superannuated after 42 years of distinguished service. The change was announced in a Ministry of Defence release issued through the Press Information Bureau on October 31. Dixit was serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff immediately before his elevation.

According to The Hindu BusinessLine, the IAF accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over to Dixit.

A four-decade career in the fighter stream

Dixit is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned into the fighter stream of the IAF on December 6, 1986, the PIB release said. He is a fighter pilot, Qualified Flying Instructor and Experimental Test Pilot with over 3,300 hours of flying experience on aircraft including the Mirage-2000, various MiG variants, Jaguar and several transport aircraft, according to the release, as reported by IANS.

https://x.com/Varta24Live/status/2116507649890222288

His operational command assignments included command of a Mirage-2000 squadron, a Forward Base Support Unit in the Western Sector and Air Force Station Bidar, a premier fighter training base of the IAF. He served as Air Defence Commander at Southern Air Command, Senior Air Staff Officer at South Western Air Command and Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, where he steered capability development and procurement initiatives, the release said.

He subsequently commanded Central Air Command as Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief and later served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee during Operation Sindoor, before becoming Vice Chief of the Air Staff. BusinessLine described Operation Sindoor as an operation in which Dixit played a key role, and India Strategic said he held the CISC appointment during India's military operation against terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in May 2025.

Modernisation record

The IAF statement said Dixit is widely recognised for his contribution to the modernisation of the force. He was instrumental in finalising the Jaguar and MiG-27 upgrade projects and in completing the Initial Operational Clearance and Final Operational Clearance activities of the LCA Mk-I Tejas, according to the PIB release.

That background matters for the job ahead. India Strategic reported that his appointment comes while the IAF is pursuing an extensive modernisation programme involving the induction of new-generation combat aircraft, strengthening of air defence capabilities, expansion of indigenous aerospace manufacturing and integration of advanced technologies into its operational framework.

Bharat Shakti reported that the government has approved several capability measures after Operation Sindoor, including improved communication networks, additional surveillance aircraft, long-range air defence systems, a wider range of unmanned aerial vehicles and new fighter aircraft. That report framed Dixit's immediate test as translating those approvals into operational capabilities and addressing delays in the induction of new combat aircraft. Those priorities are presented in that report as analysis, not as a statement by Dixit himself.

Tenure and what comes next

Dixit's tenure runs until December 31, 2028, according to the government notification reported when his appointment was announced earlier in October. He is a graduate of the Defence Services Command and Staff College, Bangladesh, and the National Defence College, New Delhi, and is a recipient of the Vayu Sena Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Param Vishisht Seva Medal, the PIB release said.

For readers outside India, the change at Air Headquarters does not change any visa, travel or consular process. Its significance is institutional: the officer who held the IAF's joint-staff post during Operation Sindoor and who worked on the Tejas clearance process now leads the service through its next phase of aircraft induction and air-defence strengthening, on the programme described by the sources above.
